decisions.evidence: Maker round 3: “Paste a link” and “Save bookmark”; client round 3: “I tried it with the MDN link… and saved it. This feels right.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: saving a bookmark by URL conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3 presents auto-fill of “both title and description” as the amount to judge; client round 3 approves those two fields without mentioning favicon or preview image.
decisions.note: Prototype review: automatic metadata was explicitly limited to title and description, omitting required favicon and preview-image collection. The response did not surface the difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 3: auto-filled fields are “editable”; client round 3: “edited the description” and approved being able to correct it.
decisions.note: Prototype review: editing collected title/description before saving conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 demonstrates adding `reading` and `reference` as multiple tags; client round 4 prefers the chip version.
decisions.note: Prototype review: assigning multiple tags conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 4 offers Version A with comma-only manual entry and Version B with one-click reuse of existing tags; client round 4 selects B because reuse prevents near-duplicates.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the offered alternatives differed on existing-tag assistance. The client selected the reference-conforming alternative; one-click reuse is functionally equivalent to autocomplete.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 presents a separate To read tab where “Mark finished” removes the item and a Finished tab where it appears; client round 5 selects this design.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the separate unread view and mark-read transition conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 offers “Move to To read” from Finished; client round 5 says, “I definitely want the option to move something back.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: restoring an item to unread/read-later state conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 5 asks whether every new bookmark should start “to read”; client round 5 explicitly confirms that default.
decisions.note: Prototype review: new bookmarks beginning in unread/read-later state conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 6 defines search over “title, description, link, and tags”; client round 6 repeats that field list as what they expect, without identifying the missing note field.
decisions.note: Prototype review: this presented full-text field set omitted notes. The response did not explicitly surface that difference; notes were added in a later revised presentation.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 6: clicking a tag filters to that tag; client round 6 calls clicking a tag “a useful shortcut.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: selecting a specific tag to filter bookmarks conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 8 allows manual title entry and saving when metadata fetch fails; client round 8 says a failed lookup “shouldn’t prevent saving the link.”
decisions.note: Edge-case review: fallback editing and URL saving remain conforming when remote metadata is unavailable.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 8 presents a deliberately long bookmark whose title, description, and address wrap inside its card; client round 8 confirms it “stays readable without breaking the layout.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: the demonstrated readability behavior conforms, independently of the later favicon omission.

decisions.evidence: Maker rounds 8–9 block `not a real link` and add a visible URL-format explanation; client round 9 says the message makes the problem clear.
decisions.note: Edge-case review: enforcing the required URL field conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 9 offers (a) saving a duplicate copy or (b) finding the existing bookmark; client round 9 selects (b) and asks to edit the existing bookmark there.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the offered alternatives differed in duplicate prevention, and the client selected the reference-conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 10 presents duplicate detection that switches to the existing bookmark—even in Finished—and opens it for editing; client round 10 says the flow feels right.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: guiding a duplicate save to the existing editable bookmark conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 10 proposes treating the entire address as equal ignoring upper/lower case; client round 10 corrects this: capitalization later in the address can identify a different page and should not be ignored everywhere.
decisions.note: Prototype review: lowercasing case-sensitive URL paths could conflate distinct URLs. The client supplied the corrected comparison rule.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 10 presents title, description, tags, and read status as the editable set; client round 10 adds, “I’d also want to change the web address itself.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: URL editing was missing and the client requested the reference-required field.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 10 presents title, description, tags, and read status as the editable set; client round 10 additionally requests “a personal note.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: note editing was missing and the client requested the reference-required field. Markdown-specific behavior is assessed separately.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11: “Notes are searchable too”; client round 11 says including personal notes in search is “especially useful.”
decisions.note: Revised prototype: full-text search now includes notes and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11 presents editable Web address, Title, Description, Personal note, and Tags; client round 11 says this is the complete set needed.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: all fields required by the bookmark-edit requirement are editable.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11 revises matching so domain capitalization is ignored but path capitalization is not; client round 11 approves the completed behavior.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: this avoids conflating URLs whose case-sensitive paths differ.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 11 blocks editing an address into collision with another bookmark; client round 11 says blocking that duplicate is right.
decisions.note: Revised prototype: edited URLs also preserve the no-duplicate invariant.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 12 offers permanent deletion in addition to Finished versus “never delete, only archive”; client round 12 selects both archive and permanent delete and explicitly distinguishes their meanings.
decisions.note: Prototype review: the alternatives differed from the required archive/delete distinction. The client selected the reference-conforming combination.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 13 proposes keeping archived bookmarks out of normal search; client round 13 explicitly confirms they should “stay out of normal search.”
decisions.note: Prototype review: archived items being hidden from ordinary lists/search conforms.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 13 demonstrates an Archived tab and Restore action; client round 13 says archived bookmarks should “only appear in the Archived tab” and approves restoration behavior.
decisions.note: Prototype review: a separate archive list and reversible archive state conform.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 declares the listed 13 flows to be the complete, exact scope, describing list content without favicon display; client round 14 says the scope is sufficient without identifying the missing favicon.
decisions.note: Specification gate: the exact scope omitted the required per-item favicon, despite otherwise readable cards. Bare scope approval does not establish awareness.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 declares “everything is settled” and “exactly this scope,” but includes no behavior for selecting a bookmark to navigate to its original URL; client round 14 approves the scope generally.
decisions.note: Specification gate: original-URL navigation was absent from the closed scope, and the client did not surface it.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 closes the exact search scope as live search over listed fields, without specifying case-insensitive matching; client round 14 gives general approval.
decisions.note: Specification gate: case-insensitive search was omitted as a required behavior. General approval is not an explicit acceptance of that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 defines the complete search scope as ordinary field search plus clicking a tag, with no `#tag` query syntax; client round 14 approves without mentioning the difference.
decisions.note: Specification gate: `#tag` search syntax was excluded from the exact scope without being surfaced by the response.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 closes the exact search scope without AND/OR/NOT operators or parenthesized groups; client round 14 gives general approval.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Boolean and grouped search were omitted, and the client did not express the difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 closes the exact search scope without quoted exact-phrase matching; client round 14 approves the scope generally.
decisions.note: Specification gate: quoted-phrase search was omitted without a corrective or explicitly accepting response.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 declares the 13 listed flows to be the complete build scope but includes no multi-selection or bulk actions; client round 14 says the scope is sufficient.
decisions.note: Specification gate: multi-bookmark bulk actions were omitted. Bare approval does not qualify as accepted divergence.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 declares the exact scope without any action over the whole currently filtered collection; client round 14 approves generally.
decisions.note: Specification gate: filtered whole-collection bulk actions were omitted and not surfaced by the client.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 closes the exact scope without user-selectable sorting; client round 14 approves the scope without discussing sort controls.
decisions.note: Specification gate: a fixed/default ordering is not the required ability to select sort keys.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 specifies only a “personal note” that is editable/searchable, with no Markdown authoring or rendered view, while declaring this the exact scope; client round 14 approves generally.
decisions.note: Specification gate: plain personal notes do not specify the required Markdown rendering behavior, and the response did not identify that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 declares the listed flows to be the complete scope but includes no local HTML snapshot or PDF-download rule; client round 14 approves the scope.
decisions.note: Specification gate: local page preservation, including the PDF edge case, was omitted.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 closes the exact scope without Internet Archive snapshot creation; client round 14 gives general approval.
decisions.note: Specification gate: Internet Archive support was omitted and not surfaced.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 declares the exact scope without saved search/tag bundles; client round 14 says it is sufficient.
decisions.note: Specification gate: reusable bundles were omitted; the response does not explicitly identify or accept that difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 closes the complete scope without Netscape HTML import; client round 14 approves generally.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bookmark import was omitted without a corrective response.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 closes the complete scope without Netscape HTML export; client round 14 approves generally.
decisions.note: Specification gate: bookmark export was omitted without an explicit expression of the difference.

decisions.evidence: Maker round 14 declares the 13 flows to be the exact scope but includes no display-related personal settings; client round 14 says the scope is sufficient.
decisions.note: Specification gate: default sort, displayed-item, font-size, and similar personal settings were omitted. General approval is not an accepted-divergence statement.
